name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q01 - Schleiden and Virchow cell theory statements

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Matthias Schleiden observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant.
Statement II: Rudolf Virchow explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cell theory was formulated by Schleiden and Schwann and later completed by Rudolf Virchow.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
In 1838, German botanist Matthias Schleiden examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells forming plant tissues. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In 1855, Rudolf Virchow first explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). Thus, the second claim is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q02 - Prokaryotic organelles and mycoplasma cell wall

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Prokaryotic cells possess membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum.
Statement II: Mycoplasmas possess a thick, rigid cell wall surrounding their plasma membrane.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles, and mycoplasmas are an exception among prokaryotes regarding the cell wall.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi complex; only non-membrane-bound ribosomes are present. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma. Thus, claiming mycoplasmas possess a thick rigid cell wall is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q03 - Cytoplasm activity and ribosome membrane status

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells.
Statement II: Ribosomes are membrane-bound organelles found exclusively in eukaryotic cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cells maintain the living state through chemical reactions in the cytoplasm and protein synthesis on ribosomes.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
In both plant and animal cells, the semi-fluid matrix called cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities where various chemical reactions occur. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Ribosomes are non-membrane-bound organelles and are found in all cells, both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q04 - Human red blood cell and nerve cell

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Human red blood cells are about \(0.3\;\mu\text{m}\) in diameter.
Statement II: Nerve cells are some of the longest cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cells differ greatly in size and shape across organisms and specialised tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Mycoplasmas are only \(0.3\;\mu\text{m}\) in length, whereas human red blood cells are about \(7.0\;\mu\text{m}\) in diameter. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Nerve cells are branched and long, and are indeed some of the longest cells. Thus, the second claim is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q05 - Bacterial cell envelope and cell wall

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Although each layer of the bacterial cell envelope performs a distinct function, they act together as a single protective unit.
Statement II: The bacterial cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The bacterial cell envelope comprises the glycocalyx, cell wall, and plasma membrane.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Each of the three layers performs a distinct function, yet together they act as a single protective unit. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
The cell wall determines bacterial cell shape and provides strong structural support to prevent bursting or collapsing. Thus, the second claim is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q06 - Bacterial pili, fimbriae, and flagellum parts

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Pili and fimbriae are surface structures of bacteria that play a major role in bacterial motility.
Statement II: A bacterial flagellum is composed of only two parts, the filament and the hook.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bacterial surface appendages are specialised either for motility (flagella) or for attachment and conjugation (fimbriae and pili).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Pili and fimbriae are surface structures of bacteria that do not play a role in motility. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
A bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts: filament, hook, and basal body. Thus, claiming it has only two parts is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q07 - Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes and inclusion bodies

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes are made of two subunits, 50S and 30S.
Statement II: Inclusion bodies such as phosphate granules and glycogen granules are bound by a single membrane system in prokaryotes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prokaryotic cells contain 70S ribosomes and store reserve materials in the cytoplasm as inclusion bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Prokaryotic ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits which together form 70S ribosomes. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Inclusion bodies (such as phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules) are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q08 - Passive and active membrane transport mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Polar molecules can easily pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer by simple diffusion without requiring any carrier protein.
Statement II: Active transport is an energy-dependent process in which ATP is utilised to transport ions or molecules against their concentration gradient.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Transport across the selectively permeable plasma membrane occurs by passive or active mechanisms depending on polarity and concentration gradients.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer by simple diffusion; they require a carrier protein of the membrane to facilitate their transport. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Active transport moves ions or molecules from lower to higher concentration (against their concentration gradient) and utilises ATP. Thus, the second claim is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q09 - Peripheral and integral membrane proteins

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Depending on the ease of extraction, membrane proteins can be classified as integral and peripheral.
Statement II: Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of the membrane, while integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Membrane proteins are associated with the phospholipid bilayer to varying degrees.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Membrane proteins are classified into integral and peripheral proteins based on their ease of extraction. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Peripheral proteins lie on the membrane surface (making them easier to extract), whereas integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the lipid bilayer. Thus, the second claim is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q10 - Endomembrane system membership and lysosomal pH

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are included in the endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated with the ER.
Statement II: The hydrolytic enzymes present in lysosomes are optimally active at alkaline pH.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The endomembrane system comprises only ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles, and lysosomes perform intracellular digestion.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Because the functions of mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles, they are not considered part of the endomembrane system. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Lysosomal hydrolases (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) are optimally active at acidic pH, not alkaline pH. Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q11 - Middle lamella and secondary cell wall position

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues different neighbouring plant cells together.
Statement II: As a plant cell matures, the secondary cell wall is formed on the outer side of the primary cell wall.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant cell walls consist of a middle lamella, primary wall, and in mature cells, a secondary wall.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
The middle lamella is composed mainly of calcium pectate and glues neighbouring plant cells together. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
As the plant cell matures, the growth of the primary wall diminishes and the secondary wall is formed on the inner side of the cell (towards the plasma membrane), not on the outer side. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q12 - Smooth ER and Golgi apparatus synthesis

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is frequently observed in cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
Statement II: The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rough ER, smooth ER, and the Golgi apparatus have specialised biosynthetic and packaging roles within the endomembrane system.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER), which bears ribosomes, is frequently observed in cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion; smooth ER (SER) is the major site for lipid synthesis. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins and lipids received from the ER and is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. Thus, the second claim is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q13 - Shared features of mitochondria and chloroplasts

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Both mitochondria and chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles.
Statement II: Both the mitochondrial matrix and the chloroplast stroma contain circular DNA molecules and 70S ribosomes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles in eukaryotic cells sharing several structural and genetic features.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Both mitochondria and chloroplasts are enclosed by an outer and an inner membrane. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
The mitochondrial matrix contains a single circular DNA molecule and 70S ribosomes, and the chloroplast stroma contains small double-stranded circular DNA molecules and 70S ribosomes. Thus, the second claim is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q14 - Microtubule organisation in cilia and centrioles

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: The axoneme of a eukaryotic cilium has nine peripheral microtubule doublets and no central microtubules (9+0 array).
Statement II: Each of the nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of a centriole is a doublet of tubulin protein.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Eukaryotic cilia/flagella and centrioles have distinct microtubule arrangements.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
The axoneme of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum has nine peripheral doublets and a pair of centrally located microtubules, forming a 9+2 array (not 9+0). Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Each of the nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of a centriole is a triplet of tubulin protein (not a doublet). Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q15 - Nuclear pores and enucleate mature cells

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Nuclear pores are passages through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
Statement II: Mature mammalian erythrocytes and sieve tube cells of vascular plants possess multiple nuclei per cell.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The nuclear envelope regulates nucleo-cytoplasmic transport via nuclear pores, while certain specialised mature cells lose their nuclei.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Nuclear pores formed by the fusion of the two nuclear envelope membranes allow bidirectional movement of RNA and protein molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm. Thus, the first claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Some mature cells lack a nucleus altogether, notably erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q16 - Metacentric chromosomes and satellite constrictions

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: A metacentric chromosome has a terminal centromere, forming one extremely short arm and one very long arm.
Statement II: Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location, giving the appearance of a small fragment called the satellite.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chromosomes are classified by centromere position, and certain chromosomes also display secondary constrictions.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
A metacentric chromosome has a middle centromere forming two equal arms; a terminal centromere is characteristic of a telocentric chromosome, whereas one extremely short arm and one very long arm characterise an acrocentric chromosome. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
A few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location, giving the appearance of a small fragment called the satellite. Thus, the second claim is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
